newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank holds interest rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank holds interest rates unchanged.

text.p: Germany's central bank decided Thursday to leave its key discount and Lombard interest rates unchanged, as economists had expected.
The Bundesbank's policy-making council decided at its regular meeting to maintain the discount rate at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate at 4.50 percent.
The bank's main money market rate, the securities repurchase, or repo, rate, was also held steady at 3 percent.

Economists had generally agreed that a cut in the bank's leading interest rates was extremely unlikely. In a Reuter poll this week all 10 economists said they expected the discount and Lombard rates to remain unchanged.

The economists said that while many recent signs about the economy have not been strong, gross domestic product should start to pick up soon, leaving the Bundesbank little reason to provide a stimulus with lower interest rates.
